entries.answer:
## Rövid válasz

Ez egy **nagy, production-szintű „Autonomous Agent Platform”** Python backend: tartós (SQLite-ban tárolt) feladatokkal, több AI-modellel, InstaVM microVM sandboxokkal, Nix környezettel, kutatási providerökkel, böngészővezérléssel, MCP/OpenAPI integrációval, HTTP/SSE API-val és webes chat felülettel.[1][2][3]

## Mi ez a projekt?

A feltöltött fájlok együtt egy **autonóm ügynök-platform** forráskódját adják. A rendszer célja, hogy egy célkitűzést (objective) és sikerfeltételeket kapjon, majd hosszú távon, újraindítás után is folytathatóan dolgozzon: tervez, eszközöket hív, ellenőriz, újratervez, gyerek-ügynököket indít, végül csak akkor ad végleges választ, ha van ellenőrzött bizonyíték.[4][5]

A platform kódverziója a konstansokban **4.2.0** körül jelenik meg, a sémaváltozat **3**, alapértelmezett HTTP host/port pedig **127.0.0.1:8765**.[2]

## Fő építőelemek

A központi osztály az `AgentPlatform`: összeköti az adatbázist, eseménynaplót, feladat-állapotgépet, artefakt tárolót, lease/heartbeat kezelést, InstaVM-et, Nix-et, kódvégrehajtást, modellroutert, research koordinátort, böngészőt, MCP-t, külső API-kat, durable tool routert, agent runnert, task coordinatort, schedulert és watchdogot.[1]

A tartós állapot **SQLite**-ban van (WAL, foreign keys, migrációk). A feladatok publikus állapotai például: queued, starting, running, waiting, sleeping, recovering, stopping, stopped, completed, error, cancelled — szigorú legális átmenetekkel.[2]

## Végrehajtási környezet

Az ügynökök **nem a helyi gépen** futnak „sima subprocess”-ként: a kód hangsúlyozza, hogy az autonóm végrehajtás **InstaVM** microVM-eken történik (`nix-dev` image), snapshot/restore/fork támogatással.[5][6]

A vendégkörnyezet **Nix**-en alapul: PATH export, flake-alapú reprodukálható toolchain, hiányzó parancsok telepítése és verifikálása, golden snapshotok.[7][8]

Van külön `CodeExecutionRuntime`, ami projekt típust felismer (Python, Node, Rust, Go, Zig, Java, .NET, stb.), majd dependencies/build/test/lint fázisokat futtat, sikernél snapshotot készít, hibánál visszaállít.[8]

## Modellek és döntési logika

A modellregistry több szerepet definiál: **glm** (végső író is), kimi, minimax, gpt (LLMAPI / Responses pipeline), mimo/mimo25/mimo25pro (Xiaomi), gemini, grok, deepseek — Requesty, LLMAPI, Gemini, MiMo útvonalakon.[9][10]

Az `AgentRunner` iteratív ciklusban dolgozik: todo.md, durable state, pontosan egy legális akció (tool / spawn / wait / sleep / merge / replan / complete), no-progress kényszerített replan, typed evidence nélküli complete elutasítása.[5]

A final response-t csak a **GLM** final writer írhatja, és csak akkor, ha minden sikerfeltételhez van ellenőrzött bizonyíték.[4][5]

## Kutatás, böngésző, eszközök

A research réteg több providert köt össze (Exa, Parallel, Valyu, Linkup, Desearch stb.), forrás-normalizálással, deduplikációval, claim–evidence gráffal.[11]

A böngésző cloud (InstaVM) és local operator módban is működik; MFA/CAPTCHA esetén emberi beavatkozásra várhat.[12]

A tool réteg széles: workspace fájlműveletek, terminal, codeexecute, nixensurecapability, sandbox snapshot/wake/restore/fork, browser, research, MCP, external OpenAPI, agent spawn/merge/verify, artefaktok.[12]

## API, web, CLI, tesztek

Van ThreadingHTTPServer alapú REST/SSE API: health/ready, tasks CRUD-szerű műveletek, stop/resume/cancel, human input, browser auth, MCP/integráció regisztráció, credential vault.[1]

A webes réteg (`ChatService`, `WebAgentPlatform`) chat sessionöket, streamelt eseményeket és static frontend kiszolgálást ad.[13]

CLI: `serve`, `task`, `self-test`. A self-test nagyon kiterjedt: parsing, DB, state machine, SSE, lease recovery, tool schema, provider kontraktusok, frontend hash védelem, „nincs artificial ceiling”, stb.[3][4]

Van egy külön, korábbi/parallel **Responses orchestration** mag is (Exa search + solve/verify/refine pipeline, tartós state file-okkal) — ezt a GPT/Responses adapter is felhasználja.[14]

## Értékelés (magyarul, őszintén)

**Erősségek.** Ez nem „demo chatbot script”. Ipari igényességű durable orchestration: idempotencia, lease, watchdog recovery, titok-redact, outbound URL biztonság, path traversal tiltás, atomic write, strict tool schema, evidence-first completion. A multi-agent + multi-model + real sandbox kombináció ambiciózus és koherens.[4][2][1]

**Komplexitás.** 15 fájl, több százezer karakter: monolitikus, sűrű, kommentmentes stílus (a self-test kifejezetten tiltja a Python kommenteket). Üzemeltetése nehéz: sok API kulcs (InstaVM, Requesty, LLMAPI, Exa, Parallel, Valyu, Linkup, Gemini, MiMo…), hálózati és számlázási függőségek.[9][4]

**Kockázatok / realitás.** A kód „production” nevet használ és élő integrációkat céloz, de a self-test élő billable hívásokat szándékosan skipeli. Sok SDK fallback/kompatibilitási ág van — ez rugalmas, de törékeny lehet provider változáskor. A biztonsági modell erős a sandbox határokon belül, de a teljes rendszer bizalmi köre nagy (külső modellek + VM API + research).[6][4]

**Gyakorlati megítélés.** Ha működő InstaVM + kulcsok + frontend megvan, ez egy **komoly autonóm kutatás/kódolás/ügynök backend**. Ha „csak futtasd le lokálisan egy fájlból” elvárásod van, túl nehéz és túl függő. Összességében: **magas színvonalú, nagyon összetett agent OS / orchestration kernel**, nem egyszerű chat wrapper.[3][5][1]

Ha szeretnéd, következő lépésként megmondhatom fájlonként, melyik modul mire való, vagy hogyan indítanád el minimális konfigurációval.

Elég részletet gyűjtöttem a rendszer teljes architektúrájáról, hogy megírjam a kért build promptot.

## Rendszerépítő prompt (teljes, önálló specifikáció)

Az alábbi egyetlen, összefüggő technikai prompt pontosan azt a rendszert specifikálja újra, amit a feltöltött fájlok tartalmaznak: egy tartós, adatbázis-alapú, több-modellű, sandbox-vezérelt autonóm ügynök-platformot.[1][2][3][4][5]

***

**PROMPT KEZDETE**

Build a durable, production-grade autonomous multi-agent orchestration backend in Python as a single cohesive package, with no simplified, mock, placeholder, or simulated components anywhere — every module must contain complete, unabridged, functioning implementation code, not stubs or TODOs.[1]

**1. Foundation layer.** Implement a configuration dataclass loaded entirely from environment variables, covering database path, state path, artifact path, host, port, timeouts, heartbeat/lease/scheduler/watchdog intervals, worker concurrency, and full credential/base-URL sets for every external integration (a sandbox/microVM execution provider, a model-routing provider, a direct LLM API provider, and five independent web-research providers). Include strict validation of every field (positive numbers, valid URLs, valid log levels, non-empty paths) and require that sandbox environments always run a fixed reproducible Linux/Nix-based image variant. Implement a structured JSON logger with level filtering and automatic secret redaction using regex patterns for API keys, bearer tokens, passwords, and cookies. Implement helper utilities: deterministic UTC timestamps, monotonic nanosecond clocks, random ID generation with prefixes, stable/sorted JSON serialization, SHA-256 stable hashing, recursive secret redaction with bounded depth, outbound URL validation that resolves DNS and blocks private/loopback/link-local/reserved IP ranges and forbidden host suffixes, URL canonicalization that strips tracking query parameters and normalizes ports, and atomic file writes using temp-file-then-rename with fsync on both the file and its parent directory.[1]

**2. Persistent storage layer.** Implement a SQLite wrapper with WAL journal mode, foreign keys enabled, full synchronous writes, and a 60-second busy timeout, wrapped in a versioned migration system that idempotently applies numbered batches of DDL statements and records applied checksums. Define a complete relational schema covering: sessions, tasks, task events (append-only sequenced event log per task), agents (hierarchical, with parent references), agent runs, model requests, tool calls and tool results, provider runs, sandboxes, Nix environment records, snapshots and snapshot lineage, browser sessions and browser authorizations, waiting states (for human-in-the-loop pauses), heartbeats, worker leases, artifacts, sources, claims, claim-evidence links, citations, webhook deliveries, idempotency records, recovery checkpoints, errors, MCP server registrations, external OpenAPI registrations, encrypted integration credentials, metrics, sandbox commands and processes, Nix capability installs, model capability cache, research branches, browser operator actions, MCP requests, and SSE connections. Every mutable table must carry an optimistic-concurrency version column, timestamps, and a trace ID; every externally-triggered write must be idempotent via a unique idempotency key column.[1]

**3. Task state machine.** Define an explicit, closed set of public task states (queued, starting, running, waiting, sleeping, recovering, stopping, stopped, completed, error, cancelled) and a hard-coded legal-transition graph; reject and log any illegal transition attempt as a persisted error before raising. Every transition must be executed inside a single atomic database transaction that also appends an event to the durable event log.[1]

**4. Durable event log.** Implement an append-only, strictly sequenced per-task event log with condition-variable-based blocking waits for new events (for streaming), full JSON-safe payload/error encoding with redaction, and support for polling from a given sequence offset with an optional limit.[1]

**5. Lease, heartbeat, and worker coordination.** Implement a single-owner lease per task with acquire/renew/release semantics based on a wall-clock expiry and a monotonically increasing generation counter, safe under concurrent workers. Implement a heartbeat table and writer that records current state, phase, current action, sandbox state, and next-action hints for tasks, agents, sandboxes, browser sessions, and worker processes, queryable by component.[1]

**6. Artifact store.** Implement a filesystem-backed artifact store rooted at a fixed directory, partitioned by task ID, with strict path-traversal prevention (reject absolute paths, `..` segments, and symlink escapes by resolving and checking containment), content-addressed via SHA-256, and metadata persisted in the database with content-type detection.[1]

**7. Encrypted credential vault.** Implement an application-level authenticated-encryption scheme (HMAC-based keystream derived via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 from a master key and a random nonce, with an HMAC-SHA256 authentication tag verified in constant time) for storing arbitrary JSON credential payloads per named scope, with expiry and revocation support — do not rely on any external encryption library.[1]

**8. Task and session service.** Implement task creation with idempotency-key deduplication, success-criteria list normalization, session auto-creation/reuse, and full task retrieval that decodes nested JSON columns and joins in child agents and artifacts. Implement stop/resume/cancel operations that also cascade state changes to all child agents and delete stale leases, plus a human-input resolution path that validates a secret resume token against its stored hash and expiry before waking the waiting task. Implement a `complete` operation that only accepts a final response from one specifically designated "final writer" model alias, rejecting completion attempts from any other source. Implement structured error recording that captures full stack traces, classifies recoverable vs. non-recoverable failures, and drives the state machine to either a recovering or terminal error state.[1]

**9. Sandboxed execution provider integration.** Implement a manager for a remote microVM/sandbox execution service accessed over an authenticated HTTP client with configurable retries, exponential backoff-aware handling of standard retryable HTTP status codes, and Retry-After header support. Implement generic SDK-compatibility shims that introspect available methods via reflection and call whichever matching method signature exists at runtime (to tolerate differing SDK versions), for provisioning, executing shell commands, snapshotting, restoring, forking, and destroying sandboxes. All autonomous code and file execution must happen exclusively inside these remote sandboxes — never as local subprocesses — and the system must hard-fail startup/execution if the sandbox provider is not configured.[5][1]

**10. Reproducible package/environment manager.** Implement a manager that provisions a declarative, pinned package-management environment (a flake-style manifest with a pinned upstream package registry reference) inside each sandbox, installs missing command-line capabilities on demand, verifies each installed capability with a minimal smoke test, and records verified capabilities in the database keyed by sandbox and command name so repeated installs are skipped.[2][1]

**11. Workspace and filesystem tool.** Implement a workspace abstraction per agent that executes a single generated Python script inside the sandbox (base64-encoded, executed via `exec`) to perform path-safe operations: mkdir, read, write, append, list, copy, move, delete, hash (single file or recursive directory tree), text search across files, in-place text patch/replace, and metadata stat — every path argument must be validated against traversal and symlink escape before use inside the sandbox script itself. Implement artifact import into a sandbox with chunked streaming, incremental hashing, and post-transfer hash verification against the artifact's stored digest.[2]

**12. Code execution runtime.** Implement a runtime that detects project type from repository contents (multiple language ecosystems), runs dependency-install, build, lint, and test phases appropriate to the detected type, snapshots the sandbox on success, and restores the last good snapshot on failure.[2]

**13. Browser automation.** Implement a browser controller supporting two modes: a cloud mode that creates and reconnects sessions through the sandbox provider's browser API (with automatic session replacement if reconnection fails), and a local operator mode that issues a single-use, time-limited, secret-token-based authorization record for human-supervised browser control. Persist all browser sessions, their external session IDs, and lifecycle state, and emit durable events for every session creation, reconnection, and authorization request; support pausing a task while awaiting CAPTCHA/MFA/manual authorization via the human-input waiting mechanism.[2]

**14. Multi-provider model routing layer.** Define a static registry mapping short model aliases to a routing provider, an underlying model identifier, and a boolean flag marking exactly one alias as the sole authorized "final writer." Support at least these role categories: a general coordination/final-writer model, an autonomous planning/decomposition model, a large-context/document-processing model, a code-analysis/debugging model, a long-document extraction model, a multimodal media-analysis model, a vision/screenshot/video-analysis model, an "unrestricted-domain" analysis model, and a mathematics/algorithms model. Each model adapter must support: structured JSON-mode generation, native provider tool/function calling, idempotency-keyed request deduplication (skip re-calling the model if an identical request was already durably recorded), and capability discovery (max input/output context sizes) cached per model.[1]

**15. Tool layer and schema validation.** Implement a hand-written JSON Schema validator (type checking including union types via `type` arrays, required properties, additionalProperties enforcement, array min/max items and item schema, string min/max length and regex pattern, numeric min/max, and enum) used to validate all tool arguments and all structured model-decision outputs against a fixed schema before they are ever executed or persisted. Implement a durable tool router that logs every tool call and its result transactionally, deduplicates via idempotency key, and restricts the callable tool set to the routing/execution stage the agent is currently in.[4][2]

**16. Research subsystem.** Implement a pluggable `ResearchProvider` interface with concrete adapters for five independent search/research services, each supporting: a `run` method that starts (or resumes, via idempotency key) a provider job, a `poll` method that checks/advances asynchronous jobs and normalizes their raw results, and a `cancel` method. Implement a source ledger that normalizes every retrieved record (URL, canonical URL with tracking-parameter stripping, title/normalized title, author, publication date, content, content hash) and deduplicates by canonical URL, content hash, or matching normalized title+domain before insertion. Implement a claim–evidence graph linking free-text claims to supporting and contradicting sources with confidence scores, provider diversity, and domain diversity counts, and only marking claims citation-eligible when backed by verifiable sources. Implement a "maximum research" orchestration loop that: builds an initial research plan (a DAG of independent sub-questions) via one model, executes all sub-questions concurrently across every configured provider in parallel "waves," ingests and deduplicates all results, runs hierarchical multi-model synthesis over batched source partitions sized to fit model context windows, extracts unresolved evidence gaps, derives new non-overlapping follow-up questions via another model, and repeats until no new unique sources or gaps are produced. Implement a citation verifier that checks every source ID referenced anywhere in a synthesis output actually exists and is citation-eligible, and flags any claim lacking a valid supporting source.[3]

**17. MCP and external API integration.** Implement an MCP (JSON-RPC based tool-server protocol) client supporting HTTP/SSE and stdio transports, server registration with credential scoping, an `initialize` handshake followed by a `notifications/initialized` call, dynamic tool/resource/prompt schema discovery and caching, and JSON-Schema-validated tool invocation with full request/response persistence. Implement equivalent registration and invocation support for arbitrary external OpenAPI-described HTTP APIs, with credential-scope-based authentication injection.[3]

**18. Agent decision loop.** Implement a durable per-agent execution loop that on every iteration: reloads durable state and rewrites a durable `todo.md` planning document inside the agent's sandboxed workspace (containing the objective, exact success criteria checklist, a numbered long-horizon plan, progress metrics, required evidence types, current phase, plan, completed/verified/active/pending actions, dependencies, blockers, failed approaches, multi-agent coordination state, and next valid actions). Compute a "no-progress" threshold from task complexity (criteria count, child-agent count, objective length) and force a mandatory replan action if consecutive no-progress iterations exceed it. Fit the full decision context (event history, plan, coordination state, todo text) into the target model's context window by externalizing low-priority historical events to sandbox files and ranking/pruning by an importance score, while always preserving the full success-criteria checklist and the most recent verification/failure/child-completion events. Require the model to emit exactly one JSON object matching a fixed decision schema (fields for reasoning, plan, long-horizon plan, progress metrics, action type, tool name/arguments, spawn-child arguments, wait/sleep reasons and resume criteria, merge target children, replan content, or completion candidate result plus completion evidence) or issue native provider tool calls (capping at exactly one tool call per iteration and rejecting excess calls). Implement a self-repair path that re-prompts the model with the specific missing/malformed schema fields whenever its output fails schema validation. Implement the legal action types: execute one tool, spawn a child agent (forking a sandbox snapshot for the child), wait for human input (creating a persisted waiting-state record with a secret resume token), sleep for a bounded duration, merge named completed child agents' results via a model call, replan, complete (only after passing verification), or stop.[4][2]

**19. Verification gate.** Implement a verifier that inspects the actual durable evidence inventory (successful terminal command executions, produced artifacts, verified browser page-state observations, citation-eligible claim-evidence links, and general tool successes) against the required evidence types for the current action, computes an objective "actual accept" boolean from that inventory alone, and then asks a model to independently confirm acceptance — final completion requires both the objective evidence check and the model's confidence to exceed a configurable minimum threshold.[2]

**20. Task coordination and scheduling.** Implement a top-level per-task run loop that: acquires the task lease, starts a background lease-renewal thread emitting heartbats, transitions the task through starting/running, requires the sandbox provider to be available (hard failure otherwise), ensures one primary agent per required model role exists (creating missing ones concurrently), runs all primary agents concurrently and waits for their completion (handling waiting/sleeping/error/cancelled sub-states by transitioning the parent task accordingly and transparently replacing failed primary or child agents from their last good sandbox snapshot), and finally synthesizes one final response — refusing synthesis if any primary agent's verified evidence is incomplete — writing it as an artifact and completing the task exclusively through the designated final-writer alias. Implement background services: a scheduler that periodically claims queued/recovering tasks up to worker concurrency, a watchdog that detects and recovers tasks/agents with stale leases or heartbeats, and a periodic provider-run reconciliation job that polls all non-terminal external research/provider jobs.[4][1]

**21. HTTP and SSE API.** Implement a threaded HTTP server exposing REST-style endpoints for health/readiness checks, task CRUD-like operations (create, get, list, stop, resume, cancel), human-input submission, browser authorization callbacks, MCP/external-API registration, and credential-vault management, plus a Server-Sent-Events endpoint that streams the durable task event log live from a given sequence offset with periodic heartbeat comments. Implement webhook receiving with per-provider signature verification and timestamp-freshness checks before processing.[1]

**22. Chat/session web layer.** Implement a chat-oriented service layered on top of the task API that manages multi-turn sessions, streams incremental events to connected clients, and serves a static frontend bundle, with the frontend's static asset hash pinned and verified at startup to prevent silent tampering.

**23. Command-line entry points.** Implement a CLI with three subcommands: `serve` (start the HTTP/SSE server and background services), `task` (create and run a single task from the command line, printing the final response), and `self-test` (an extensive internal test suite covering configuration parsing, database migrations and schema integrity, state-machine legality, SSE event streaming, lease expiry and recovery, JSON-Schema tool-argument validation, every research provider's contract methods, credential-vault round-trip encryption, artifact path-traversal rejection, outbound URL security rejection of private/internal addresses, atomic-write crash safety, and an explicit assertion that no artificial capability ceilings, hard iteration caps, or feature-limiting shortcuts exist anywhere in the codebase). The self-test suite must skip only genuinely billable live external API calls, while exercising every other code path against real logic with no mocked internal behavior.[4][1]

Write the entire system as production-ready, fully implemented Python modules with no omitted logic, no placeholder functions, and no reduced-scope substitutes for any described component. Every module must be directly executable and internally consistent with every other module described above, sharing the single database, event log, configuration object, and logger instance.

**PROMPT VÉGE**
